common_prompt:
Create one exceptional professional character concept sheet for an original MERIDIAN operative in 2043, a realistic dark near future. Use both supplied Cutline and Overlap reference images for their shared tactical construction language; develop the specified new design. Keep athletic adult human proportions, compact head and shoulders, restrained load carriage, and credible shallow composite armor over textile. The character must visibly carry more armor than either reference while remaining mobile.

Use a landscape sheet: dominant full-body front three-quarter at left, smaller matching full-body rear centrally, enlarged closed helmet detail at upper right, compact subjective in-helmet HUD study below it. Keep both figures' entire heads and boot soles inside generous margins. Match helmet, plate seams, closures and materials across views. Stand naturally with arms slightly separated and empty gloved hands. Show no weapon. Use a neutral warm-gray background, controlled material painting, readable shadows, subtle wear, graphite composite, muted olive or ash fabric, and dark practical boots. English header: MERIDIAN / 2043. Add the specified ID and name.

Show articulated chest, back, flank and abdominal protection, compact outer shoulder plates, forearm guards, thigh armor, distinct knee caps and shin plates. Keep visible textile flex zones at neck, armpits, elbows, waist, hip creases, knees, wrists and ankles, plus clear rifle-stock seats. Avoid oversized pauldrons, rigid limb tubes, powered armor, exoskeletons, armor skirts and gadget clutter.

Completely conceal face, eyes and skin: opaque black visor, closed shallow hard mask, sealed textile collar and gloves. Integrate the helmet computer into small temple or occipital volumes with recessed service seams and protected display optics behind the visor. No external electronics box, exposed cables, luminous face, hologram or power core.

Label the HUD inset HUD STUDY / PROPOSAL. Show an unobstructed forward view into plain neutral space, sparse dim peripheral brackets and one small abstract menu mark, without a human face or cutaway. These are speculative local interface marks: no targeting, sensing, anomaly readout, numerical telemetry, command contact, orders or ability indicators. The helmet is ordinary equipment; personal abilities do not originate in it.

variants.name: Datum
variants.design_summary: Cutline-derived crown strip and paired jaw frame above octagonal core plates with three articulated abdominal bands.
variants.prompt: 16 / DATUM. Develop Cutline's clipped carrier into a cropped octagonal breastplate with a matching upper back plate. Beneath each, three broad shallow bands overlap toward the belt, with independent flank leaves sliding behind them. Add compact single shoulder caps, tapered forearm shells, one short outer plate per thigh, separate knee caps and narrow shin guards; retain a broad textile break above every knee. Keep belt pouches few and low. Build the helmet around a separate central crown strip joining two rounded side panels, a broad trapezoid black visor and paired shallow jaw panels meeting under the chin. Set a flush computer access pocket into the right temple, continuing inside the shell; keep the left side visually quiet. Give the visor rim a protected recessed optical seam. Show the rear band articulation and temple pocket consistently in the detail. Keep the whole assembly close to the body.

variants.name: Traverse
variants.design_summary: Overlap-derived diagonal jaw and crown seam paired with two diagonal breast leaves and staggered abdominal tabs.
variants.prompt: 17 / TRAVERSE. Extend Overlap's diagonal construction into two broad breast leaves crossing along one restrained oblique lap, followed by two short staggered abdominal tabs ending above the hip creases. Carry the diagonal overlap across the upper back, with independent lower back and flank segments. Avoid a hanging torso flap. Use two small overlapping outer shoulder leaves, oblique forearm guards, short outer thigh shields, separate compact knees and tapered shin plates. Construct a compact helmet with an offset crown seam, narrow continuous opaque visor and two closed jaw shells overlapping diagonally across the lower face. House the computer inside the thicker rear temple on the same side as the upper jaw leaf; describe its presence with a recessed service outline, never a bolt-on box. Let ash edge bindings separate graphite plates from olive textile. Make diagonal armor layering legible at full-body scale while keeping both stock seats open.

variants.name: Laminate
variants.design_summary: Two overlapping helmet shells and a nape computer strip echo broad transverse torso lames and segmented limb guards.
variants.prompt: 18 / LAMINATE. Use four broad transverse composite lames to cover the chest and upper abdomen, with shallow overlaps and staggered ends wrapping onto flexible flank carriers. Repeat the four-level construction on the back, stopping cleanly above a soft waist. Avoid tiny repetitive scales. Place two compact lames on each outer shoulder, divide forearm guards into two broad segments, and use two horizontal thigh overlaps above independent knee and shin caps. Keep the inner limbs and joint folds textile. Form the helmet from a front brow cap overlapping a rounded rear crown shell, with a straight opaque visor band and a one-piece shallow jaw closure. Recess the computer's service strip into the nape just above the collar; retain the reference helmet's overall size. In the detail, distinguish the cap overlap, protected visor rim and quiet rear service seam. Use restrained graphite surfaces over ash-olive fabric.

variants.name: Splitline
variants.design_summary: A divided crown and paired temple housings accompany longitudinal breast and back halves with a covered central lap.
variants.prompt: 19 / SPLITLINE. Organize the armor longitudinally: two long breast halves meet over a covered narrow central lap, then separate into paired short abdominal plates above the belt. Use independent left and right scapular plates over a flexible covered back seam, with small lumbar panels and segmented flanks. There is no open gap over the sternum. Compact shoulder caps, divided outer forearm shells and slim paired thigh panels continue the vertical language; isolate the knees and shins with clearly visible textile gaps. Construct the helmet from left and right crown shells meeting along one recessed sagittal seam, without a raised crown rail. Give it a squared black visor with short angled side returns and paired shallow cheek-to-chin panels. Integrate low temple computer housings symmetrically beneath the shell edges. Show their flush service seams in the helmet detail. Keep the central seams quiet and the shoulder width human.

variants.name: Mantle
variants.design_summary: A brow hood and separate closed jaw cradle accompany a cropped pectoral yoke, suspended rib shields and short belly plate.
variants.prompt: 20 / MANTLE. Build the torso from a short shallow pectoral yoke ending inside the shoulder joints, two independently suspended vertical rib shields beneath it, and a separate cropped belly plate. Cut generous stock-seat recesses beside the yoke. On the back, a compact upper yoke supports two short lumbar leaves; segmented flank plates preserve twisting space. Add restrained outer shoulder caps, short segmented hip-to-thigh guards, two-piece forearms, isolated knee caps and slim shin plates. Keep the hip creases clear, without a skirt. Give the helmet a shallow projecting brow hood over a recessed panoramic opaque visor and a separate closed U-shaped jaw cradle. The cradle encloses the lower face completely. An integrated horseshoe service seam around the rear shell suggests the internal computer without increasing head width. Show a soft neck bellows below the hard shell. Use graphite armor, olive textile and only a few belt pouches.

variants.name: Keel
variants.design_summary: A compact jaw wedge and cheek-integrated computer echo swept rib plates converging around a narrow sternum insert.
variants.prompt: 21 / KEEL. Compose the breast armor around a narrow sternum insert flanked by two broad swept rib plates, all shallow and closely fitted. Their lower edges converge into three short tapered abdominal segments rather than a single rigid belly. On the rear, paired upper planes meet a tapered central back plate above an articulated lumbar guard; keep the sides segmented. Use small clipped shoulder caps, tapered outer forearm shells, narrow thigh shields and separate knee and shin elements. Leave the inner thigh and back of each knee visibly textile. Construct a compact angular helmet dome with a trapezoid black visor and a short central jaw wedge between two flat cheek returns. The wedge remains shallow, without a beak or snout. Recess the computer behind the left rear cheek return and show a small protected service seam. Echo the torso's convergence in helmet seams, without symbols, lights or a central device.

variants.name: Course
variants.design_summary: A separate visor-and-mask cassette and occipital hatch pair with broad torso plates arranged in staggered courses.
variants.prompt: 22 / COURSE. Use two broad courses of torso plates, each course comprising two low-profile overlapping panels. Offset the vertical joint between courses so the chest reads as four substantial surfaces rather than a conventional single carrier or fine scales. Continue staggered joints around compact flank plates; show paired upper back panels and a two-plus-one lumbar arrangement. Small shoulder caps, offset outer thigh tiles and divided forearm guards extend this construction. Keep separate knees and shins, with soft joint gaps. Form a one-piece faceted helmet cap around a visibly separate front cassette containing the opaque visor and fully closed shallow mask. Outline that cassette with one restrained U-shaped recessed seam. Fit a small rectangular computer access hatch flush into the occipital shell above the collar. Keep display optics protected within the visor rim. Show the cassette seating and rear hatch consistently, using graphite plates over subdued olive and ash textile.

variants.name: Offset
variants.design_summary: A lateral helmet closure and flush temple slab echo wraparound torso shells with side closures and offset belly leaves.
variants.prompt: 23 / OFFSET. Replace the diagonal carrier with one broad shallow breast shell that wraps partly around the ribs and closes through a lateral overlap on the wearer's left. Beneath it, three offset belly leaves articulate above the belt. Give the back shell a corresponding side closure and separate lower back segments. Keep a slim soft waist and very short hip leaves. Use two small shoulder leaves on the left and one compact cap on the right, with both stock seats clear; add tapered forearms, short thigh plates, independent knees and narrow shin armor. Build the helmet with a continuous low brow, a lateral shell closure, a black visor and a fully closed mask with a horizontal chin seam. Set one flush computer access slab inside the rear temple contour. Echo the side closure in the rear helmet view. Keep asymmetry structural and restrained, without extra equipment bulk.

variants.name: Facet
variants.design_summary: A three-plane opaque visor and faceted mask echo four broad kite-shaped torso panels and flexible flank wedges.
variants.prompt: 24 / FACET. Arrange four broad low-relief kite-shaped composite panels across the chest and upper abdomen over a continuous protective textile carrier. Use their blunt intersecting edges to create structure, with no central emblem, device or exposed opening. Flexible flank wedges connect to four broad triangular rear panels with independent lumbar articulation. Add compact angular shoulder caps, diamond-cut outer forearm and thigh guards, and separate blunt knee and shin pieces; preserve clear textile movement zones. Construct the helmet with quadrilateral crown panels, a single opaque visor folded into three shallow planes, and a closed three-facet lower mask. Keep the temples and jaw within a compact human silhouette, without spikes or exaggerated cheek fins. Recess a small computer service panel into the rear shell; the visor's inner edge protects its display optics. Paint graphite planes with subtle value differences over muted olive textile, keeping the broad panel geometry readable.

variants.name: Chevron
variants.design_summary: An overlapped crown and chevron brow accompany three broad nested torso chevrons with sliding flank ends.
variants.prompt: 25 / CHEVRON. Develop three broad nested blunt chevrons through the chest and abdomen, each a shallow overlapping composite segment with sliding ends at the flanks. The lowest ends above the soft waist. Repeat the three-part chevron construction across the back with readable gaps for articulation. Use compact two-leaf outer shoulder guards, oblique forearm plates, paired short outer thigh shields, separate knee caps and tapered shin guards. Keep all inner limb bends textile, with no rigid connections crossing joints. Construct the helmet from a low central crown cap overlapped by two side shells. Give the opaque visor a shallow chevron brow edge, and close the lower face with a horizontal jaw panel and diagonal cheek returns. Recess twin computer service seams into the rear shell instead of adding a rear pack. Keep the design close to Overlap's restrained graphite-and-olive equipment language. Show nested overlaps clearly in both body views.
